description: This topic explores the composition of air, the role of oxygen in combustion and burning, and how iron rusts and can be protected from rusting.

mcq.questionText: Which gas makes up the largest percentage of clean dry air by volume?
mcq.explanation: Nitrogen makes up about 78% of air by volume, which is far more than any other gas present.

mcq.questionText: Approximately what percentage of air by volume is oxygen?
mcq.explanation: Oxygen makes up about 21% of air by volume and is the active part that supports combustion and breathing.

mcq.questionText: Which part of air is described as the active part because it supports burning?
mcq.explanation: Oxygen is the active part of air because it is the gas needed for substances to burn.

mcq.questionText: What is the main gas produced when carbon-containing fuels burn completely in air?
mcq.explanation: Complete combustion of a carbon-containing fuel in plenty of oxygen produces carbon dioxide.

mcq.questionText: In an experiment, the volume of air in a tube fell after iron filings were left to rust. By about what fraction did the air decrease?
mcq.explanation: Rusting uses up the oxygen, which is about one fifth (21%) of the air, so the air volume falls by roughly one fifth.

mcq.questionText: Which two substances must both be present for iron to rust?
mcq.explanation: Rusting requires both oxygen (from air) and water; if either is absent, iron will not rust.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following is NOT a method of preventing iron from rusting?
mcq.explanation: Leaving iron in damp air provides both water and oxygen, which speeds up rusting rather than preventing it.

mcq.questionText: The chemical name commonly given to rust is:
mcq.explanation: Rust is hydrated iron(III) oxide, formed when iron reacts with oxygen and water.

mcq.questionText: When a burning splint is lowered into a gas jar and it goes out at once, the gas is most likely:
mcq.explanation: Carbon dioxide does not support burning, so it puts out a lighted splint, which is the test for this gas.

mcq.questionText: Which gas relights a glowing splint, confirming it is oxygen?
mcq.explanation: Oxygen supports combustion strongly, so it relights a glowing splint, which is the standard test for oxygen.

mcq.questionText: About what percentage of air is made up of the noble gases such as argon?
mcq.explanation: The noble gases, mainly argon, make up roughly 1% of the air by volume.

mcq.questionText: Combustion is best described as a chemical reaction in which a substance reacts with oxygen and releases:
mcq.explanation: Combustion is the reaction of a substance with oxygen that releases energy mainly as heat, and usually light too.

mcq.questionText: A candle burning under an upturned glass jar soon goes out. The best explanation is that:

options.text: The oxygen inside the jar has been used up
The jar has cooled the flame

mcq.explanation: Burning uses up the limited oxygen trapped in the jar, and once it is gone the candle cannot continue to burn.

mcq.questionText: Galvanising protects iron from rusting by coating it with a layer of:
mcq.explanation: Galvanising coats iron with zinc, which keeps out air and water and also corrodes in place of the iron.

mcq.questionText: Which substance is commonly placed in a tube together with iron in rusting experiments to keep the air dry?
mcq.explanation: A drying agent such as anhydrous calcium chloride removes water vapour, so the iron stays dry and does not rust.

fib.questionText: The most abundant gas in air, making up about 78% by volume, is _____.
fib.explanation: Nitrogen is the most plentiful gas in the air at roughly 78% by volume.

fib.questionText: The active part of air that supports combustion is the gas called _____.
fib.explanation: Oxygen is the active part of air because it is needed for substances to burn.

fib.questionText: The slow reaction of iron with oxygen and water to form a reddish-brown solid is called _____.
fib.explanation: Rusting is the gradual corrosion of iron when it is exposed to both oxygen and water.

fib.questionText: A chemical reaction in which a substance reacts with oxygen to release heat and light is called _____.
fib.explanation: Combustion, or burning, is the reaction of a substance with oxygen that gives out heat and usually light.

fib.questionText: The gas that turns limewater milky and does not support burning is _____.
fib.explanation: Carbon dioxide turns limewater milky and puts out a burning splint, which are its standard tests.

fib.questionText: Oxygen makes up about _____ percent of air by volume.
fib.explanation: Oxygen forms approximately 21% of the air by volume.

fib.questionText: Coating iron with a thin layer of zinc to prevent rusting is called _____.
fib.explanation: Galvanising protects iron by covering it with zinc, which keeps out air and water.

fib.questionText: Both oxygen and _____ must be present for iron to rust.
fib.explanation: Iron rusts only when both oxygen and water are present; removing either one prevents rusting.

fib.questionText: In a rusting experiment, the volume of air decreases by about one _____ because oxygen is used up.
fib.explanation: Since oxygen is about one fifth of air, using it up reduces the air volume by roughly one fifth.

fib.questionText: Burning with a limited supply of oxygen can produce a poisonous gas called carbon _____.
fib.explanation: Incomplete combustion, where oxygen is limited, produces poisonous carbon monoxide instead of carbon dioxide.

tf.questionText: Nitrogen is the most abundant gas in air.
tf.explanation: Nitrogen makes up about 78% of air, more than any other gas.

tf.questionText: Oxygen makes up about 78% of the air by volume.
tf.explanation: Oxygen is about 21% of air; it is nitrogen that is about 78%.

tf.questionText: Carbon dioxide supports the burning of a wooden splint.
tf.explanation: Carbon dioxide does not support burning; it actually puts out a lighted splint.

tf.questionText: Iron can rust even when it is kept completely dry and away from water.
tf.explanation: Rusting needs water as well as oxygen, so dry iron does not rust.

tf.questionText: Painting iron helps to prevent it from rusting.
tf.explanation: A layer of paint keeps air and water away from the iron surface, preventing rusting.

tf.questionText: Combustion is a chemical reaction that releases heat.
tf.explanation: Combustion is a reaction with oxygen that releases energy mainly as heat, and often as light.

tf.questionText: During rusting in a sealed tube, the level of water rises because oxygen in the air is used up.
tf.explanation: As oxygen is consumed by rusting, the air volume falls and water rises to take its place.

tf.questionText: Rust is a hard, shiny coating that protects iron from further damage.
tf.explanation: Rust is a flaky reddish-brown solid that crumbles away, exposing fresh iron to further rusting.

tf.questionText: A glowing splint bursts into flame when placed in oxygen.
tf.explanation: Oxygen relights a glowing splint, which is the standard laboratory test for the gas.

tf.questionText: Salt water makes iron rust more slowly than fresh water does.
tf.explanation: Salt water speeds up rusting, so iron near the sea rusts faster than in fresh water.

summary.correctAnswer: Air is a mixture of about 78% nitrogen, 21% oxygen, 1% noble gases, and small amounts of carbon dioxide and water vapour.
summary.explanation: Knowing the main gases and their rough percentages is the foundation of this topic.

summary.correctAnswer: Oxygen is the active part of air because it supports combustion and is needed for living things to breathe.
summary.explanation: Oxygen, about one fifth of air, is what makes burning and respiration possible.

summary.correctAnswer: Combustion is a chemical reaction in which a substance reacts with oxygen to release heat and usually light.
summary.explanation: Combustion always involves oxygen and gives out energy.

summary.correctAnswer: Oxygen relights a glowing wooden splint.
summary.explanation: This simple test identifies oxygen because the gas strongly supports burning.

summary.correctAnswer: Carbon dioxide turns limewater milky and puts out a lighted splint.
summary.explanation: These two observations together confirm the presence of carbon dioxide.

summary.correctAnswer: Iron rusts only when both oxygen and water are present.
summary.explanation: Removing either oxygen or water stops the rusting process.

summary.correctAnswer: Rust is hydrated iron(III) oxide, a reddish-brown flaky solid formed when iron corrodes.
summary.explanation: Rust forms on the surface and flakes off, exposing more iron to attack.

summary.correctAnswer: Rusting can be prevented by painting, oiling, greasing, galvanising, or coating iron with another metal.
summary.explanation: These methods work by keeping air and water away from the iron surface.

summary.questionText: Experiment to find the active part of air
summary.correctAnswer: When iron is left to rust in a closed tube of air, the air volume falls by about one fifth as oxygen is used up.
summary.explanation: The one-fifth decrease shows that oxygen is the active part and makes up about 21% of air.

summary.correctAnswer: Complete combustion of a fuel in plenty of oxygen gives carbon dioxide, while incomplete combustion in limited oxygen gives poisonous carbon monoxide.
summary.explanation: The amount of oxygen available decides which products are formed.

hoq.questionText: A student sets up four test tubes with iron nails: Tube 1 has dry air only, Tube 2 has boiled water with oil on top (no air), Tube 3 has ordinary water and air, and Tube 4 has water with dissolved salt and air. In which tube will the nail rust the fastest?
hoq.explanation: Tube 4 has oxygen, water and salt; salt speeds up rusting, so this nail rusts fastest of all.

hoq.questionText: When a piece of magnesium ribbon is burned in air and the white ash collected weighs more than the original ribbon, the best explanation is that:

options.text: Some air was trapped inside the ash
The magnesium combined with oxygen from the air to form magnesium oxide
Heat added mass to the magnesium

hoq.explanation: During combustion the magnesium gains mass because it combines with oxygen from the air to form magnesium oxide.

hoq.questionText: A candle is fixed in a dish of water and lit, then covered with an upturned glass jar. The flame goes out and water rises a little way up the jar. The rise in water level is mainly because:

options.text: All the gas in the jar was used up
The oxygen used in burning was replaced by the rising water
The wax pushed the water up

hoq.explanation: Burning uses up the oxygen (about one fifth of the air), reducing the gas volume so water rises to fill the space left.
